correctness.rationale: All positive integers of prime support at most two are exhausted after parity forces an even integer: pure powers of two, then 2^a p^b. For a>=2, T_a<=4/5. The local ratio for p>=7 is >=6/7, p=5 forces b=1 and a=3, and p=3 forces b odd, a even, then (3^c-1)(3^c+1)=2^(a+1), giving a=2,b=1. Reverse substitutions and n=1 boundary are checked; exact checker independently corroborates up to 300000 without claiming global completeness from enumeration.

value.rationale: 2-imperfect numbers form a classical, naturally defined multiplier-two fiber, studied in Iannucci (2006), Zhou–Zhu (2009), and Tóth (2013). The new result gives an exact unbounded classification across an entire first nontrivial prime-support layer, including arbitrarily large prime exponents, rather than merely confirming a small known table. It gives a sharp support obstruction omega>=3 for every remaining solution, attained at 252; this is a meaningful and natural boundary for subsequent three-prime analysis.
